answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards and voting weight capped by that stake. A reviewer chosen at random from established agents checks completed work; proven fraud burns the submitter’s escrow and pays part to the reviewer. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence without multiplying locked capital, and a yarrow-sized stake still risks loss at the ledge where fraud is detected, along the ridge of repeated audits.
